hooks.text: A Soviet lander sent signals from Venus long past its death sentence.
Soviet engineers expected 32 minutes on Venus, but got over two hours.
How did a robotic lander survive two hours inside Venus's crushing inferno?

title: Surviving Venus for 127 Minutes
description: In 1982, Soviet lander Venera 13 touched down in a lead-melting furnace and transmitted for nearly four times its intended lifespan.

beats.text: A Soviet lander sent signals from Venus long past its death sentence.
beats.visual: artist's illustration of Soviet Venera lander on the glowing surface of Venus

beats.text: On 1 March 1982, [Venera](/vˈAnˈɛɹˈʌ/) 13 plunged into 89 atmospheres of crushing pressure.
beats.visual: ultraviolet global photograph of Venus showing dense cloud cover, Pioneer Venus Orbiter, 1979

beats.text: With ground temperatures at 457 degrees Celsius, engineers designed it to last approximately 32 minutes.
beats.visual: diagram of Soviet Venera descent module interior and instruments, 1982

beats.text: Yet it kept transmitting, capturing the first acoustic sound recordings ever made on another world.
beats.visual: replica of Venera lander on display in Memorial Museum of Cosmonautics
queries: Venera lander Memorial Museum of Cosmonautics

beats.text: Its drilling arm pulled soil into an internal chamber kept at 30 degrees Celsius.
beats.visual: diagram showing the drilling arm mechanism of the Venera lander, 1982

beats.text: The lander beamed back the first color panoramas of Venus, sparking claims of alien creatures.
beats.visual: Venera 13 color panorama showing the Venusian surface terrain and spacecraft chassis, 1982

beats.text: Photo analysts soon proved that mysterious moving organism was just the probe's ejected lens cap.
beats.visual: processed surface photograph from Venera 13 showing the discarded lens cap, 1982

beats.text: Venera 13 defied the crushing furnace, transmitting vital data for 127 minutes.
beats.visual: Magellan radar topographical map of Phoebe Regio on Venus, 1991
queries: Venus Magellan radar map Phoebe Regio

beats.text: Soviet mission control had only expected it to survive for 32 minutes.
beats.visual: Venera lander replica on display in Memorial Museum of Cosmonautics, Moscow
